title: Ultrametric summability criterion and bound for arbitrary families
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value $|\cdot|:K\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$, complete for $d(a,b)=|a-b|$. For any set $I$ and family $u:I\to K$, summability means convergence of the net $S\mapsto\sum_{i\in S}u_i$ over finite subsets $S\subset I$, ordered by inclusion. The family is summable if and only if for every $\epsilon>0$ the set $\{i\in I:|u_i|\ge\epsilon\}$ is finite. If it is summable and $C\ge0$ satisfies $|u_i|\le C$ for all $i$, then $|\sum_{i\in I}u_i|\le C$. These statements include empty and finite index sets.
